experiments.question: Does Rugg's table and grille, its table drawn from the Voynich's own fragments, write text that behaves like the Voynich?
experiments.prediction: Word lengths and slot fit match (built in); line effects, adjacent repeats and near repeats fail, since grille and table know no line
experiments.controls: the Voynich development text (reference); the carried text itself where there is one
experiments.measurements: ENT.h2 WL.mean WL.share TYPE.ratio REP.adjacent LINE.first LINE.last NEAR.edit1 SLOT.fit NOVEL
experiments.tolerances: the Voynich's own Currier A-B spread, at least a tenth of its pooled value (candidates.py judge)
experiments.rejection: any required measure outside its tolerance
experiments.result: 3262 lines, 25642 words; 3 of 10 measures match; fails: ENT.h2, TYPE.ratio, REP.adjacent, LINE.first, LINE.last, NEAR.edit1, NOVEL

experiments.question: Does Hannig's grid read the repeated words of the development pages into Hebrew more often than it reads the same text shuffled?
experiments.prediction: With 2-4 letters per sign for several signs and vowels unwritten, short Hebrew skeletons are hit often by chance; the real text no higher than its shuffles
experiments.controls: the same grid on the Voynich units shuffled across the text, word lengths kept, 20 shuffles
experiments.measurements: read share of repeated word types; unreadable share
experiments.tolerances: the pass bar: over 0.80 and above the highest shuffle
experiments.rejection: read share at or under the highest shuffle, or under 0.80
experiments.result: 0.214 of 1933 repeated word types read into hebrew-torah (18617 types); 0.072 unreadable (a sign with no value); chance line, highest of 20 shuffles, 0.321 (median 0.311); examples sheey=$wA x96; dsheor=wsr x2; shor=sr x76; qokeol=ykl x33; shol=sl x132; qokeeol=ykl x6; chor=nr x161; shey=&A x193
